chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) by entering into Ihram for Hajj after Umrah, entered Mecca, performed Tawaf and Sa'i, put on his clothes, and exited Ihram, but forgot to shorten his prayer (of four rak'ahs) until he went out to Arafat. He said: There is no harm with him.
He builds upon the Umrah and its Tawaf, and the Tawaf of Hajj follows after it.

key_terms.سَعَى: Performed Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mutamatti' forgets to shorten prayers after Umrah but before Arafat?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who forgets to shorten prayers after exiting Ihram for Umrah but before departing for Arafat incurs no penalty. The ruling emphasizes the validity of the Umrah's Tawaf and establishes that the Hajj's Tawaf is performed subsequently, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle of leniency in cases of forgetfulness during ritual transitions. This highlights the distinction between obligatory acts and recommended acts in the sequence of Hajj rituals within the Ja'fari school.
